newsitem.title: USA: Disney agrees to buy Mammoth Records.
newsitem.headline: Disney agrees to buy Mammoth Records.

text.p: Walt Disney Co has agreed to purchase Mammoth Records, an independent label.
Industry sources valued the deal at up to $25 million.
As part of the deal, Mammoth's founder and president, Jay Faires, will enter into a five-year employment contract and will continue to serve as Mammoth's president.
Faires started Mammoth in 1988 after graduating with a master of business administration degree from Duke University.
Mammoth will be part of a music group that also includes Disney's struggling Hollywood Records and a newly launched Nashville label, all to be distributed by PolyGram NV.
"Jay Faires has quietly built one of the most widely admired record companies in the industry," said Joe Roth, chairman of Walt Disney Studios.

Based in Carrboro, N.C., with offices in New York, Los Angeles and London, Mammoth has a roster of more than 25 artists, including the gold-record-selling Squirrel Nut Zippers as well as Frente!, The Backsliders and Pure.
Mammoth also has a catalog of about 120 albums.

In 1995, as part of a previous joint venture, Faires became vice president of artists and repertoire at Time Warner Inc's Atlantic Records and signed several artists, including the platinum act Seven Mary Three.
